title: How the schooling got him the Fletcher Henderson job
summary: His reading and phrasing training let him play first trumpet with Fletcher Henderson with no rehearsal when Pop Smith quit.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I'll tell you. By him doing that, I got a break. I got one of the biggest breaks in my life. That's how I became known, by him making me do that. I come to New

York and I -- Pop Smith was with Fletcher Henderson and he quit. [He up to bad.] So someone told Fletcher about me. I was working with Chick Webb then, but Chick wasn't working. So he came by and asked Chick could I go to work with him. And Chick said, 'Yeah, I'll let you have him to go out on this trip.' So I went with Fletcher. No rehearsal or nothing. Playing first trumpet.
First trumpet. In that band. That was really a tall order, wasn't it?

It sure was. So if I hadn't been schooled properly, I never would have made it. No rehearsal or nothing. First job, put the music in front of me, and I just played it just like it was, you know, A, B, C.

Well, Cootie, you must have -- I mean there's a question of the way that band phrased and everything. You at least were familiar with the sound of that band, weren't you? You were familiar with it, weren't you? You had heard the band.
Yeah. His music was marked. The phrasing -- all the phrasing was marked through there. And so I went and played it --
Like it was there.
Just like it was. You know, by being under my teacher, and he made me phrase and do the things -- the marking of the music.
Yeah. Yeah.
And that paid off.
Yeah. That's wonderful. That really is. Well, listen, we won't -- that's another period that we'll be coming to.
Yeah.
So we won't go into that.
Okay.

We'll go back. Well, one thing though, like -- as you were studying like seven or eight years with him, what did he have you doing? Did he have you playing trumpet parts or big parts? I mean, how did he keep bringing you on all the time?
Well, sometimes me and him would play duets.
Oh, you would.
Yeah. Duets.
That was good. Yeah.
We played duets.
